questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad):
1. It comprises the United States, India, Japan and Australia.
2. It is a formal military alliance with a mutual defence clause.
3. It was revived in 2017 at a meeting held in Manila.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Quad was first mooted in 2007 on Japanese initiative and lapsed in 2008. It was revived in November 2017 on the margins of the ASEAN meetings in Manila, but it remains a consultative grouping with no mutual defence obligation, unlike NATO.
questions.h: Quad = US + India + Japan + Australia, a dialogue, not a treaty.

questions.q: Under Pillar I of the AUKUS partnership, the United States and the United Kingdom are to help Australia acquire:
o: a shared fleet of aircraft carriers
hypersonic missiles for the Australian army
questions.e: AUKUS, announced in September 2021 by Australia, the UK and the US, centres on nuclear-powered submarines, not nuclear-armed ones, for Australia. Pillar II covers advanced technologies such as AI, quantum and hypersonics.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about BRICS:
1. The acronym BRIC was coined by Jim O'Neill of Goldman Sachs in 2001.
2. The first BRIC summit was held at Yekaterinburg in Russia in 2009.
3. South Africa joined the grouping in 2010.
4. The New Development Bank has its headquarters in Moscow.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: BRIC began as an investment-bank label, became a diplomatic forum with the Yekaterinburg summit, and added South Africa in 2010 to become BRICS. The New Development Bank is headquartered in Shanghai.
questions.h: B-R-I-C: Brazil, Russia, India, China, then S-outh Africa made the S.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries became a full member of BRICS on 1 January 2024?
questions.e: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE joined on 1 January 2024 after the invitations issued at the Johannesburg summit. Argentina declined its invitation, Indonesia became a full member only in January 2025 and Mexico is not a member.

questions.q:
Match the exercises with the countries with which India conducts them.
Exercise: A. Dharma Guardian  B. Mitra Shakti  C. Nomadic Elephant  D. Ajeya Warrior
Country: 1. Mongolia  2. United Kingdom  3. Japan  4. Sri Lanka
questions.e: Dharma Guardian is the India-Japan army exercise, Mitra Shakti is with Sri Lanka, Nomadic Elephant is with Mongolia and Ajeya Warrior is with the UK.

questions.q:
Which of the following pairs correctly match India's bilateral army and special forces exercises with the partner countries?
Exercise: A. Yudh Abhyas  B. Shakti  C. Harimau Shakti  D. Garuda Shakti
Country: 1. France  2. Indonesia  3. United States  4. Malaysia
questions.e: Yudh Abhyas is the India-US army exercise and Shakti the India-France one. Harimau Shakti is with Malaysia (harimau means tiger) and Garuda Shakti with Indonesia.
questions.h: Harimau = tiger in Malay, so Harimau Shakti is Malaysia.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an exercise and the country with which India conducts it is NOT correctly matched?
o: Naseem Al Bahr : United Arab Emirates
questions.e: Naseem Al Bahr is the India-Oman naval exercise, whereas the India-UAE naval exercise is Zayed Talwar. Varuna (France), Konkan (UK) and SIMBEX (Singapore) are correctly matched.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Malabar naval exercise:
1. It began in 1992 as a bilateral exercise between India and the United States.
2. Japan became a permanent participant in 2015.
3. Australia became a permanent participant along with Japan in 2015.
4. It is held exclusively in the Arabian Sea.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Malabar started as an India-US exercise, and Japan became a permanent participant in 2015. Australia took part again in 2020, completing the Quad in the exercise, and the venues have included the Bay of Bengal, the Pacific and the Arabian Sea.

questions.q: Which one of the following multilateral exercises is hosted by the Indian Navy?
questions.e: MILAN began in 1995 at Port Blair and is held by the Indian Navy, with recent editions at Visakhapatnam. RIMPAC is held by the US near Hawaii, Pitch Black by Australia and Cobra Gold by Thailand and the US.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of exercises and countries:
1. Surya Kiran : Nepal
2. Ekuverin : Sri Lanka
3. Sampriti : Myanmar
4. Lamitiye : Thailand
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Surya Kiran is the India-Nepal army exercise. Ekuverin is with the Maldives, Sampriti with Bangladesh and Lamitiye with Seychelles.

questions.q:
Match the thinkers with their concepts.
Thinker: A. Halford Mackinder  B. Nicholas Spykman  C. Alfred Thayer Mahan  D. Friedrich Ratzel
Concept: 1. Sea power  2. Heartland theory  3. Lebensraum  4. Rimland theory
questions.e: Mackinder argued that whoever controls the Heartland of Eurasia commands the world, Spykman countered with the Rimland, Mahan stressed sea power, and Ratzel developed Lebensraum (living space).
questions.s: Standard IR texts; NCERT Class 12, Contemporary World Politics
questions.h: Mackinder = land (Heartland); Mahan = sea; Spykman = the rim.

questions.q: The term 'Malacca Dilemma' refers to:
o: India's dependence on the Strait of Malacca for its Pacific trade
the dispute among littoral states over piracy patrols in the strait
Malaysia's difficulty in regulating shipping through the strait
China's vulnerability due to dependence on the Strait of Malacca for energy imports
questions.e: Chinese President Hu Jintao used the phrase in 2003, pointing to the risk that a hostile power could choke the strait through which much of China's oil passes. It is one reason for China's ports, pipelines and the Belt and Road projects.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of doctrines and their descriptions:
1. Monroe Doctrine : The US would not oppose European colonisation of the Americas
2. Truman Doctrine : US aid to Greece and Turkey to resist communism
3. Brezhnev Doctrine : Soviet right to intervene in socialist states
4. Marshall Plan : Soviet economic programme for Eastern Europe
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Monroe Doctrine (1823) warned European powers against new colonisation in the Americas, so the pair reverses it. The Marshall Plan was a US programme for Western European recovery; the Soviet counterpart was Comecon.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12, Contemporary World Politics Ch 1; standard IR texts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Peace of Westphalia (1648) is regarded as the foundation of the modern system of sovereign states.
Statement-II: It established the principles of territorial sovereignty of states and non-interference in their internal affairs.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The treaties ending the Thirty Years' War recognised each ruler's authority over his territory, which became the basis of the state system. So Statement-II explains why Statement-I holds.

questions.q: At the launch of the Indo-Pacific Economic Framework for Prosperity (IPEF) in 2022, India did NOT join which one of its pillars?
questions.e: India joined the pillars on supply chains, clean economy and fair economy, and stayed out of the trade pillar, taking observer status there. The reasons given were its concerns on labour, environment and digital trade.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a signatory to the memorandum of understanding on the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) announced at the 2023 G20 Summit?
questions.e: IMEC was announced at New Delhi in September 2023 by India, the US, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, the EU, France, Germany and Italy. Iran is outside the corridor.

questions.q: Which of the following groupings is known as the 'West Asian Quad'?
questions.e: I2U2 groups India, Israel, the UAE and the US, hence the 2 and 2 in the name. IBSA is a South-South grouping of India, Brazil and South Africa.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the United Nations:
1. The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945.
2. The International Court of Justice is the only principal organ of the UN not located in New York.
3. The Trusteeship Council has been abolished by an amendment to the Charter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 and came into force on 24 October, now UN Day. The ICJ sits at The Hague. The Trusteeship Council suspended operations in 1994 after Palau became independent, but the Charter still lists it.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12, Contemporary World Politics Ch 4; un.org

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN Security Council:
1. The ten non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly for two-year terms.
2. The abstention of a permanent member amounts to a veto.
3. Five of the ten non-permanent seats are allotted to African and Asia-Pacific states together.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: A resolution fails only if a permanent member casts a negative vote, and abstention allows it to pass if nine votes are in favour. Three seats go to Africa and two to Asia-Pacific.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12, Contemporary World Politics Ch 4; un.org

questions.q: India's term in 2021-22 as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council was its:

Consider the following statements about the International Court of Justice (ICJ):
1. Its judges are elected by the General Assembly alone.
2. Its judges serve nine-year terms and one-third of the Court is renewed every three years.
3. No two judges may be nationals of the same state.
4. All members of the UN are ipso facto parties to the Statute of the Court.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Judges are elected by the General Assembly and the Security Council independently, each by an absolute majority. The Court has 15 judges on nine-year terms, no two of the same nationality, and the Statute is annexed to the Charter.

questions.q:
Match the UN bodies with their headquarters.
Body: A. UNEP  B. UNHCR  C. FAO  D. UNIDO
Headquarters: 1. Rome  2. Vienna  3. Nairobi  4. Geneva
questions.e: UNEP is in Nairobi, UNHCR in Geneva, FAO in Rome and UNIDO in Vienna.
questions.h: Nairobi = Nature (UNEP); Geneva = refugees; Rome = food; Vienna = industry.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN Human Rights Council:
1. It replaced the Commission on Human Rights in 2006.
2. Its members are elected by the Security Council.
3. It is a subsidiary body of the General Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Council, with 47 members, is elected by an absolute majority of the General Assembly, to which it reports. Unlike the Commission, which was under ECOSOC, it works through the Universal Periodic Review.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the crimes covered by the Responsibility to Protect (R2P) doctrine adopted at the 2005 World Summit?
questions.e: R2P covers genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity. Natural disasters are outside its scope.
questions.s: un.org (Office on Genocide Prevention and R2P)

questions.q: Which UN mission, set up in 1949, monitors the ceasefire line in Jammu and Kashmir?
o: UN Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan
questions.e: UNMOGIP was set up after the Karachi Agreement of 1949. UNTSO, created in 1948, was the first UN peacekeeping mission, in the Middle East.
questions.h: UNTSO 1948 was first; UNMOGIP 1949 is the Kashmir one (Karachi Agreement).

questions.q: UN Security Council Resolution 1325 (2000) deals with:
o: non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction to non-state actors
questions.e: Resolution 1325 recognised the impact of war on women and called for their participation in peace processes. Counter-terrorism financing was dealt with in Resolution 1373, and WMD non-proliferation to non-state actors in Resolution 1540.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):
1. There are seventeen SDGs.
2. They were adopted at the Rio+20 conference in 2012.
3. They replaced the Millennium Development Goals, which had ten goals.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The 2030 Agenda with 17 goals was adopted by the UN General Assembly in September 2015. The Rio+20 conference of 2012 launched the process, and the MDGs (2000-2015) had eight goals.

questions.q: The Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC) of the United Nations has how many members?
questions.e: ECOSOC was enlarged from 27 to 54 members in 1973, elected by the General Assembly for three-year terms. The Security Council has 15 members and the Human Rights Council 47.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The General Assembly can recommend collective measures to restore peace when the Security Council is deadlocked by a veto.
Statement-II: The 'Uniting for Peace' resolution of 1950 allows the Assembly to meet in an emergency special session in such a situation.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Resolution 377 (V) of 1950 was passed during the Korean War to bypass Soviet vetoes. It supplies the procedure that makes the Assembly's action in Statement-I possible.

questions.q: Under the UN Charter, the Secretary-General is appointed by:
o: the General Assembly on the recommendation of ECOSOC
the five permanent members of the Security Council
the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council
questions.e: Article 97 provides for appointment by the General Assembly on the Council's recommendation, so a permanent member's veto can block a candidate. The term is five years and renewable.
questions.h: GA appoints, SC recommends: so the veto reaches the choice.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Uniting for Consensus group, which opposes new permanent seats on the Security Council:
1. Italy is a leading member of the group.
2. Pakistan is a leading member of the group.
3. Brazil is a member of the group.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Uniting for Consensus (the 'Coffee Club') favours more elected seats rather than new permanent ones, opposing the G4 bid of Brazil, Germany, India and Japan. Italy and Pakistan are among its prominent members.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT among the five founding members of ASEAN in 1967?
questions.e: ASEAN was founded by the Bangkok Declaration of 1967 by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand. Brunei joined in 1984, soon after becoming independent.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the East Asia Summit (EAS):
1. Its first summit was held in 2005.
2. India was not among the original participants.
3. The United States and Russia joined in 2011.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The first EAS in Kuala Lumpur (2005) included India, Australia and New Zealand along with ASEAN, China, Japan and South Korea. The US and Russia joined at the 2011 summit.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC):
1. Its first summit was held at Dhaka in 1985.
2. Its Secretariat is located in Kathmandu.
3. The SAARC Charter allows bilateral and contentious issues to be taken up.
4. Afghanistan was a founding member.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: SAARC was launched at Dhaka in 1985 with seven members and has its Secretariat at Kathmandu. The Charter excludes bilateral and contentious issues, and Afghanistan joined only in 2007.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about BIMSTEC:
1. Its Secretariat is located in Dhaka.
2. Pakistan and the Maldives are members.
3. It links countries of South Asia and Southeast Asia.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: BIMSTEC has seven members: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. Pakistan and the Maldives are not members, and the grouping bridges South and Southeast Asia.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The United Kingdom left the European Union on 31 January 2020.
Statement-II: The UK invoked Article 50 of the Treaty on European Union to start the withdrawal process.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 50 TEU is the exit clause, and the UK triggered it in March 2017 after the 2016 referendum. The exit followed from this process, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about NATO:
1. Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty has been invoked only once, after the 11 September 2001 attacks.
2. Sweden joined NATO before Finland.
3. NATO headquarters is located in Brussels.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Article 5 on collective defence has been invoked once, after the 9/11 attacks. Finland joined in April 2023 and Sweden in March 2024.

questions.q: The African Union, launched in 2002 as the successor to the Organisation of African Unity, has its headquarters at:
questions.e: The OAU was founded in 1963 at Addis Ababa and the AU, launched at Durban, kept the city as its seat. The AU Commission is housed there.

questions.q: The League of Arab States, formed in 1945, has its headquarters at:
questions.e: The Arab League was set up in Cairo, where it is based today. The Gulf Cooperation Council, formed in 1981, is separate and sits at Riyadh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO):
1. It evolved from the Shanghai Five and was founded in 2001 with Uzbekistan joining the original five.
2. India and Pakistan became full members in 2017.
3. Its Secretariat is located in Beijing.
4. Afghanistan is a full member of the SCO.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Shanghai Five (1996) became the SCO in June 2001 with Uzbekistan's entry. India and Pakistan joined at Astana in 2017 and its Secretariat is in Beijing; Afghanistan has been an observer.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the Mekong-Ganga Cooperation?
questions.e: MGC, launched in 2000, comprises India, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam. It is named after two rivers that are cradles of civilisation.
questions.h: Mekong-Ganga = India + the five CLMVT-style neighbours (Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam); Malaysia is missing.

questions.q: The European Union was formally established by the:
questions.e: The Maastricht Treaty, signed in 1992, came into force in 1993 and created the EU. The Treaty of Rome (1957) set up the EEC, the Lisbon Treaty (2007) reformed the EU's institutions, and Schengen deals with border-free travel.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP)?
questions.e: RCEP groups the ten ASEAN states with China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand. India withdrew from the negotiations in November 2019 over concerns about trade deficits and market access.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) came into force in December 2018.
Statement-II: The United States withdrew from the Trans-Pacific Partnership in January 2017, after which the remaining members concluded the CPTPP.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The CPTPP is the reworked TPP of the remaining eleven countries after the US exit, so the withdrawal explains the new agreement.

questions.q: India is NOT a member of which one of the following?
questions.e: India has wanted APEC membership but the group has had a moratorium on new members, so India is not a member. It is a member of the EAS, the ARF and the G20.

questions.q: Which agreement replaced the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) in July 2020?
questions.e: The US-Mexico-Canada Agreement entered into force on 1 July 2020. NAFTA had operated since 1994.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a founding member of Mercosur under the Treaty of Asuncion (1991)?
questions.e: Mercosur's founders were Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. Chile is only an associate state.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Asian Development Bank (ADB):
1. It is headquartered in Manila.
2. It was established in 1966.
3. Its presidents have traditionally been Japanese.
4. India is a founding member of the bank.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: ADB was set up in 1966 and sits at Manila. Japan and the US are its largest shareholders, and India has been a member since its founding.

questions.q: The Secretariat of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) is located at:
questions.e: The AfCFTA Secretariat is in Accra, Ghana, though the African Union itself sits in Addis Ababa. Trading under the AfCFTA began on 1 January 2021.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The United States has an effective veto over major decisions at the IMF.
Statement-II: Major IMF decisions require an 85 per cent majority of total voting power, and the United States holds more than 15 per cent of it.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Because the US holds roughly 16 per cent of votes, no decision requiring 85 per cent can pass without it. So Statement-II explains Statement-I.
